description:
STATUS CHANGE (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1): this is now a LIVE WRONG
ANSWER, not a compile failure. The interp door compiles samelambda3 and
prints 12.0 / 11.0 where the program means 12 / 11.0 -- in BOTH call
orders (swapped: 11.0 / 12.0; the int call is always wrong). Native
refuses: "closure capture 0 of callable 69 has no single settled
representation" (the fz-kdt.125 ClosureCapture layout guard). The earlier
interp compile failure ("omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs
semantic inputs") is gone -- some landing in the mailbox family
(130/152/155) removed the refusal and exposed the miscompile beneath it.
Repro (session scratchpad sl3.fz):

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  end
  fn main() do
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(1), 10))     # means 12   -- prints 12.0
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(0.5), 10))   # means 11.0 -- prints 11.0
  end

THE MECHANISM, traced end to end (this is where the "confusion" between
two closures of DIFFERENT type is manufactured):

1. mk(1) and mk(0.5) are one lambda L with capture types int and float:
   closure[L](int) and closure[L](float). Instantiated, their signatures
   DIFFER ((int)->int vs (int)->float). The type system carries that
   difference in the CAPTURE of the closure literal; the lambda's own
   arrow stays polymorphic in n until a (capture, arg) pair is analyzed.
2. run only FORWARDS f. World::canonical_activation_key (world.rs:1846):
   a non-recursive body whose keying does not consume callable identity
   gets Types::erase_transported_closure_identities (types/mod.rs:866),
   which for every DispatchDemand::Ignore slot replaces the closure
   literal with erase_closure_identity(param). That erases the literal
   WHOLE -- identity AND captures -- to a bare polymorphic arrow. Dump:
     key P.run/2[fp[F] (a0_p0) -> a0_r, fp[int] int]
   ONE key for run; the int/float difference is gone from the key.
3. Inside that one body the per-row evidence stays precise, so run's
   callsite twice(f, x) mints TWO targets:
     P.twice/2[closure[L](float), int]   (x16, return lane RawF64)
     P.twice/2[closure[L](int),   int]   (x17, return lane RawInt)
   with the lambda specialized at all four [capture,arg] combinations.
4. The dispatch between them has NO question. Dump of run's plan:
   "dispatch miss=Unreachable ... arm a0 -> o0 proofs=[] projections=[]
   ... graph root=n1; n1 outcome o0". The root node IS outcome 0: no test
   is emitted, because the only runtime handle is fn_id (identical) and
   nothing reads the capture. Arm 0 (the float body) takes every value.
5. The int closure therefore runs inside twice[float]. The interp's
   dynamic arithmetic still computes 11 and 12 as ints, but the body's
   return lane is RawF64, so the int result is marshaled through a float
   lane and comes out 12.0. Silent, deterministic, wrong.

So the signatures do differ; the KEY threw the difference away, and the
runtime cannot rebuild it. Nothing at dispatch can fix step 4 for this
shape without a capture read; the defect is in step 2's erasure being
too coarse.

TWO SUB-POPULATIONS, TWO CURES (verified 2026-09-02):

(A) captures differ in TYPE -- samelambda3 (int vs float). Zero corpus
    occurrences, constructible from ordinary source, wrong answer today.
    CURE AT THE KEY: erase_transported_closure_identities must erase the
    closure literal's IDENTITY but keep its capture TYPES, i.e.
    closure[?](int) vs closure[?](float) stay distinct keys. Then run has
    two bodies, each callsite has ONE twice target, no dispatch, no lane
    coercion, no representation change, and fz-6gb's sharing is
    preserved for every same-typed literal. The erasure must recurse into
    captures (erase identities inside captured closures too) so that
    population (B) keeps sharing -- otherwise the 32-reducer fanout
    fz-6gb was built to kill returns. Check the erase_closure_identity
    call graph for other callers that rely on the whole-literal erasure.

(B) captures differ only in IDENTITY -- the six residue groups
    (00231, 00277 x2, 00281, opaque_fn_value_join,
    repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2). Verified on 00281:
      Enum.reduce/3#lambda[fnref[add_a/2], int, int]
      Enum.reduce/3#lambda[fnref[add_b/2], int, int]
    where add_a and add_b are textually identical (int,int)->int; the
    forwarders List.reduce_cont/3 and reduce_step/3 are keyed at an
    erased variable a2. Type-preserving erasure still (correctly) merges
    these forwarders, so the callsite still holds N targets. Here the
    runtime CAN separate them: the identity axis (fz-kdt.125) recursing
    ONE level into the capture slot -- load capture 0, test its code
    word -- the same per-position recursion fz-kdt.119 landed for tuples.
    In 00281 the reducer is chosen by a runtime case, so a runtime
    question is genuinely required; the corpus cannot see today's arm-0
    fiat only because add_a and add_b compute the same thing.

The ticket's earlier "NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER" comment measured only
population (B) (00281 with acc-x); it does not cover (A). The earlier
'unrepresentable plan' DIAGNOSTIC backstop remains refuted as a cure
(it would refuse five corpus fixtures) and is at most the residue policy
for whatever (A)+(B) leave.

RELATIONS: fz-kdt.137 (depth-1 tuple instance of the compile-failure
half); fz-kdt.119(3) enlarges (B)'s population one tuple deep; fz-6gb
consume-keying is the design being narrowed by (A); fz-kdt.125 identity
axis is what (B) extends. Sequence: (A) first (it is the wrong answer),
(B) second, then re-run the indistinguishable-arm residue gate
(drive_test.rs INDISTINGUISHABLE_ARM_RESIDUE) expecting 6 -> 0.

ACCEPTANCE: samelambda3 prints 12 / 11.0 on interp, JIT and AOT in both
call orders; a red-first three-path test with production paths;
00281 twin changed to acc - x still -6 on all paths; residue gate 6 -> 0
after (B); fz-6gb's sharing census unchanged for same-typed literals
(executable counts on its fixtures do not rise); canon movement
classified.

comments.text:
MEASURED by the fz-kdt.125 build (2026-09-01, base bd03d922e). Two premises in
this ticket's body and in fz-kdt.125's spec item 6 are REFUTED:

(1) "13/13 in-corpus groups are identity-separable" is an artifact of the
census helper. Its separability test regexes EVERY closure/fnref name out of a
key, including the ones sitting in CAPTURES -- and a capture is not identity.
Re-measured against the landed axis: the no-question population falls 13 -> 6,
not 13 -> 0. The 6 survivors are THIS ticket's shape exactly, same fn id and
different captures:

  00231_joined_fn_refs_enum_reduce      1  closure[Enum.reduce/3#lambda](fnref[add_a/2])
                                           vs (fnref[add_b/2])
  00277_enum_tier0_fixture              2  same lambda over two different inner closures
  00281_opaque_reducer_closure          1  as 00231
  behavior/opaque_fn_value_join         1  as 00231
  behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2  1  as 00277

(2) "Corpus fallout of the backstop measured ZERO" therefore does not hold. An
unrepresentable-plan DIAGNOSTIC on inseparable groups would refuse to compile
five corpus fixtures. The fz-kdt.125 build did NOT land it for that reason --
the routing half of this ticket is still open and still unbuilt, and it needs
either capture discrimination or a corpus that stops relying on the shape.

WHAT DID LAND, and it is this ticket's ABI half: `Prim::ClosureCapture` reads a
capture back out of a closure through the boundary that WROTE it, and refuses
at compile time when one callable was minted at several capture layouts that
disagree about a slot -- which is samelambda3's shape. That turns "native
executable lowering failed for index 11" into a named invariant failure. The
compile failure itself (interp: "omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs
semantic inputs") is untouched and still this ticket's.

NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER, measured: 00281 with its twin function changed from
`acc + x` to `acc - x` answers -6 on interp and JIT at head. The six groups'
arm-0-takes-all is order-decided but the members are interchangeable on the
probes tried; that is luck, not a proof.

fz-kdt.119 review sequencing (2026-09-01): 119(3)'s recursive identity-preserving erasure ENLARGES this ticket's population ({:tag,#66(int)} vs {:tag,#66(float)} collapse to one question at depth -- same-fn-id/different-capture, one tuple deep). Also this ticket's compile-failure half now has a depth-1 instance with its own ticket (fz-kdt.137) which blocks 119's REFNEST-style acceptance. The backstop-policy decision this ticket owns grows correspondingly.

title: P1: a forwarder's activation key erases a transported closure's CAPTURE TYPES, not just its identity -- same lambda at int/float captures gives a WRONG ANSWER on interp (12.0 for 12) and a refusal on native
